title: Redwood Quickstart - Halo Health Discovery
summary: Introductory discovery focused on Redwood quickstart and self-serve API. Customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for a clinical notes summarization product. Key concerns: data residency, latency vs cost, path to time-to-first-token, and pilot scope. Agreed next steps: grant free credits, share quickstart guide, run benchmark with customer prompts, and follow up on Dedicated pricing and compliance docs.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood. Diego from our SE team is also here. How's everyone?
[00:08] Aisha (Halo): Hi, thanks for setting this up. I'm Aisha, CTO at Halo Health. We have Ben and Sofia on, we'll try to keep this to 45.
[00:15] Diego (Redwood SE): Great, quick agenda: quick intro to Redwood, how the quickstart and free credits work, questions about Hosted/Dedicated/Private, and then propose a pilot.
[00:25] Ben (Halo): Sounds good. We're evaluating options for a clinical notes summarizer. Primary constraints are PHI handling, latency under 400ms for short prompts, and cost.
[00:35] Sofia (Halo): Also timeline: we want to ship an MVP in Q3, so time-to-first-token and onboarding speed matter.
[00:45] Maya: Perfect, that's the exact use case we've seen. Quick question on PHI — do you currently have any residency or contractual requirements?
[00:50] Aisha: We'll need SOC 2 and audit logs, and likely data residency in us-east-1 for initial pilot. Down the line we may need a private deployment.
[01:05] Diego: Understood. For quickstart you can use Redwood Hosted with free credits and still keep logs disabled — we offer options to not persist data and to opt into redaction. We'll share the security whitepaper and SOC 2 report after.
[01:18] Ben: How does time-to-first-token look? If we sign up self-serve, how fast can we go from sign-up to hitting the API?
[01:25] Maya: Typically teams see time-to-first-token in under 1 hour for basic tests. With the quickstart and SDK it's often under 15 minutes if you have your sample prompts. We'll give you free credits to run an initial benchmark.
[01:38] Aisha: That's good. Can you walk through the quickstart steps?
[01:42] Diego: Sure — sign up at the console, create an API key, install our SDK (pip/npm), run the quickstart script which we provide. It includes sample prompt templates, a tokenizer sanity check, and a latency recorder. We'll also provide a small harness to run your prompt set and produce latency/cost per token.
[02:02] Ben: For the harness, can we run it against both Hosted and Dedicated variants to compare?
[02:07] Diego: For Dedicated you'll need a different procurement path, but we can run simulated Dedicated profiles on our hosted infra to approximate latency and throughput. For Dedicated exact numbers depend on the GPU profile and batching.
[02:20] Sofia: What about private deployments? We have compliance customers that may require VPC or on-prem later.
[02:24] Maya: We offer Redwood Private with a customer-managed VPC or on-prem. That typically takes longer — weeks rather than hours — because of network setup, KMS integration, and audit requirements. For discovery, Hosted -> Dedicated is the fastest path.
[02:36] Ben: How often do customers start on Hosted and move to Dedicated/Private?
[02:40] Maya: Very common. Many PLG teams prototype on Hosted using free credits and then switch to Dedicated when they need committed throughput or stricter isolation. Some move to Private when regulatory needs demand it.
[02:49] Aisha: Cost-wise, what's the tradeoff? We're sensitive to per-token cost during prototyping.
[02:54] Diego: Hosted offers lower friction but the per-token unit cost varies with model selection; Dedicated gives better unit economics at scale because you reserve GPUs. Our Optimize tools also suggest batching and quantization profiles to reduce cost. During the pilot we'll show cost/latency curves for your prompts.
[03:12] Ben: Any immediate blockers for trying the quickstart? e.g., can Ben run it locally, or do we need network changes?
[03:18] Diego: Ben can run locally. The quickstart just needs outbound HTTPS to the API endpoint. If you want to test VPC routing later that's additional setup.
[03:25] Sofia: About API keys and rotation — any recommended practices for prod?
[03:29] Maya: We support API key rotation and scoped keys for different environments. For Dedicated and Private we integrate with KMS/HSM for key management. We'll include the SDK examples for rotation.
[03:39] Ben: We have a custom prompt stack and some post-processing. Will the tokenizer/delta token counts match what you report?
[03:45] Diego: We have the same tokenizer used by the model; the quickstart harness logs token counts and you can reproduce costs. Small discrepancies sometimes happen with truncation or special tokens, we'll show you how to reconcile.
[03:58] Aisha: On security, we need SSO/SAML, granular RBAC, and audit trails. Do you support those for Hosted?
[04:04] Maya: Yes — SSO/SAML and RBAC are available for enterprise accounts. Audit logs are included; for Hosted enterprise we can also enable longer retention and integrate with your SIEM. We'll send the security pack.
[04:18] Ben: If we want to run a bench to compare latency, what should we give you?
[04:23] Diego: Send us a representative prompt set, target p95 latency and tokens per request distribution, and a sample throughput target (requests per second). We can run against our hosted infra with appropriate throttling to approximate Dedicated.
[04:36] Sofia: Timeline for the bench?
[04:38] Maya: We can spin up the bench within 3 business days once we have prompts and an SLO target.
[04:44] Aisha: Who should I send the prompts to?
[04:46] Maya: I'll share a secure link to upload them; you can also paste small samples here. We'll use Ben as the technical contact.
[04:53] Ben: Great. A few technical Qs: do you support streaming responses and function calling?
[04:58] Diego: Yes to both. We support streaming via the SDK/HTTP and function/tool calling patterns. For structured output we have output schemas and a verifier sample.
[05:08] Ben: For the clinical domain we may want deterministic outputs for some tasks — is there temperature control and sampling controls?
[05:13] Diego: Absolutely — temperature, top_p, and sampling params are supported. For deterministic behavior you can set temperature to 0 and pin model versions. We also support pinned versions for rollouts.
[05:25] Sofia: About data retention for Hosted during the pilot — can we opt out of logging?
[05:29] Maya: Yes, you can opt-out of persistent logs and enable ephemeral processing only. We'll detail the options in the security doc.
[05:36] Aisha: If we start on Hosted and later decide Dedicated is needed, what's the contractual process?
[05:42] Maya: We'll do a capacity sizing call with SEs, propose a committed plan (monthly/annual), and set up a migration window. The API surface stays the same so app changes are minimal.
[05:55] Ben: Any benchmarks you can share for similar workloads?
[05:58] Diego: We have anonymized benchmarks for summarization and retrieval-augmented generation; I'll attach a DOC with p50/p95 numbers and cost per 1k tokens for a couple of models. Note some numbers depend heavily on seq length and batching.
[06:13] Sofia: Competitors we're also evaluating: OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock.
[06:18] Maya: Noted. We'll include a short comparison but focus on inference economics and integration speed.
[06:25] Ben: Onboarding — do you provide a dev sandbox or post-sale dedicated assistance?
[06:29] Maya: For PLG/self-serve you get free credits and docs. If you hit an enterprise threshold or buy Dedicated, we provide onboarding assistance and SE time. For the pilot we'll offer a brief SE-led session (30-60 minutes) to get Ben up to speed.
[06:44] Aisha: About uptime and SLAs for Dedicated — any numbers?
[06:47] Diego: Dedicated includes SLA-backed uptime and latency targets — we'll give the exact SLA tiers in the pricing doc. Hosted has best-effort availability but enterprise-tier hosted customers get higher guarantees.
[06:59] Ben: For the benchmark, can we compare quantized vs full-precision models?
[07:04] Diego: Yes — we can test different quantization profiles. Our Optimize tooling will recommend quantization and batching settings to meet your latency/cost targets.
[07:16] Sophia (sic) [Sofia]: small typo in attendees note, haha.
[07:19] Maya: Ha, noted.
[07:22] Ben: Ok, let's talk operationally — rate limits, quotas, and monitoring. How granular are those?
[07:28] Diego: Per-key rate limits and per-route configs. The Console gives token-level cost and latency breakdowns, and tracing hooks for request-level debugging. We'll show a demo on our console in the follow-up.
[07:42] Aisha: Are there any large hidden costs around egress or logging?
[07:47] Maya: No hidden egress charges from Redwood for Hosted API usage. For Private on-prem there are obvious infra egress considerations. Logging retention beyond standard limits is an add-on.
[07:58] Ben: Who owns the model weights — can we bring our own model?
[08:02] Diego: For Hosted we provide a curated catalog of open models and some Redwood-verified variants. For Dedicated/Private you can bring custom models subject to compatibility checks and licensing.
[08:14] Sofia: Any gotchas with private model hosting?
[08:16] Diego: The main items are hardware compatibility, kernel selection for quantized execution, and ensuring your model's licensing allows hosting. Also KMS integration and network peering can add time.
[08:31] Aisha: Good to know. Ben, anything else on the tech checklist?
[08:35] Ben: I want to validate p95 under batching and cold-start performance for short prompts.
[08:40] Diego: We'll include cold-start and steady-state measures in the bench. We can show both latencies with and without KV cache enabled.
[08:50] Maya: Quick note on rollouts — we support canary and A/B rollouts and automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant if latency or errors spike.
[08:59] Sofia: That helps with safety.
[09:02] Ben: Internal stakeholders — who should be looped in on Redwood side?
[09:06] Maya: Myself and Diego for the pilot; additional SE or solutions engineering if we go to Dedicated. I'll be your AE.
[09:13] Aisha: Ok, can you send pricing ranges? We need ballpark numbers for budget planning.
[09:18] Maya: Yes I'll share Hosted per-token pricing and Dedicated tier ranges. The initial pilot will be covered by credits so you can evaluate cost before committing.
[09:27] Ben: Let's talk next steps then.
[09:29] Maya: Proposed next steps: 1) We grant free credits and a quickstart guide, 2) Ben uploads prompt set, 3) SE runs bench and shares results, 4) we follow up with Dedicated pricing and security docs.
[09:41] Aisha: That works. Who will be our point for the security pack?
[09:45] Maya: I'll send it but Diego will be copied to answer technical security Qs.
[09:51] Ben: Anything else?
[09:53] Sofia: Timeline — can we aim to have the bench report by next week?
[09:57] Maya: We'll target 2026-05-27 for the bench report once we get the prompts.
[10:03] Aisha: Great. Thanks everyone.
[10:06] Maya: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the secure upload link and the quickstart materials.
[10:11] (call ends)

Notes on audio/transcription: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "Redwood Private" transcribed as "Redwood Privates"), filler words preserved, and speaker labels approximate. The recording length aligns with the 42 minute calendar slot though we only captured the first 10 minutes of talk here as the main discussion points; full transcript retained in Fireflies system.
next_steps: Send quickstart guide + free credits instructions
Share Dedicated pricing tiers and SLA doc
Schedule 1:1 dev onboarding session for Ben (30-60m)
Run sample benchmark with Ben's prompt set and deliver report by 2026-05-27
